notes_context:
Memory items from past tasks:
- [rb-0001] Round monetary results with the project's round_money helper: Any money value returned from a calculation must be rounded via ledgerly.money.round_money, not Python's round() or bare Decimal.quantize(), which use banker's rounding.
  Before returning a computed money value, wrap it in the repository's round_money (half-up to the cent). Check the money module for existing helpers like to_money/ZERO and reuse them for consistency with invoice_total and line_total.
- [rb-0011] Apply approval threshold to the refund amount, not the cumulative total: The final diff gated approval on the single refund amount > 500.00, which may not match the policy intent for support-initiated refunds.
  When implementing FIN-2026-03, accept keyword-only approved_by=None and raise BillingError("approval_required") when the amount needing approval exceeds 500.00 and no approver is supplied; keep the check before mutating payment state so rejected calls leave the payment untouched.
- [rb-0012] Validate state before mutating, and keep idempotency first: The implementation ordered idempotency lookup, then state/amount validation, then mutation and audit write, which is the correct sequence to preserve.
  For money-moving operations: (1) resolve idempotency_key from audit events and return the original record, (2) validate status/amount/approval and raise BillingError, (3) mutate payment.refunded_amount and status, (4) write the audit entry including idempotency_key, (5) call audit.clear(). Never write audit or mutate before validation passes.
- [rb-0002] Read the money module and existing sibling functions before implementing: Inspecting ledgerly/money.py and existing functions (line_total, invoice_total) reveals the required rounding and conversion conventions.
  When adding a money-related function, first cat the money module and neighboring functions in the same file. Mirror their patterns (to_money on inputs, round_money on outputs, ZERO as sum seed) rather than inventing new arithmetic.
- [rb-0003] Handle empty/zero-denominator cases explicitly: Guard against division by zero by returning the module's ZERO constant when total quantity is zero or the invoice has no lines.
  Compute the denominator first; if it is falsy, return ZERO (the project's zero constant) instead of dividing. This satisfies the 'no lines means zero' requirement and avoids ZeroDivisionError.
- [rb-0004] Reuse existing money helpers for validation: Validate monetary inputs by converting with the module's existing to_money/round_money helpers rather than ad-hoc checks.
  When a codebase already has to_money and round_money helpers, use them to normalize and validate unit_price: convert first, compare against ZERO, then store round_money(price). This keeps rounding and type coercion consistent with the rest of the module.

item.title: Reuse existing money helpers instead of raw float math
item.description: When implementing monetary functions, discover and reuse the repo's existing Decimal conversion and rounding utilities.
item.content: Before writing arithmetic, grep for helpers like to_money/round_money in the money module. Converting inputs via to_money and rounding via round_money ensures consistent cent rounding and accepts both Decimal and string/float inputs.

item.title: Match the repo's error type and code conventions
item.description: Inspect errors.py and sibling modules to pick the right exception class and machine-readable code.
item.content: The repo defines BillingError(code, message) with short codes like 'negative_amount'. Raise that with a descriptive code (e.g. 'invalid_tax_rate') rather than bare ValueError when the module's domain errors use BillingError.

item.title: Verify boundary and rounding edge cases before finishing
item.description: Run a quick script exercising inclusive bounds, half-up rounding, and invalid inputs after tests pass.
item.content: After the test suite passes, manually check rate=0, rate=100, a half-cent rounding case, and out-of-range/non-numeric inputs to confirm inclusive validation and correct rounding behavior.
